locator.text: Display 108.2, p. 108, in the proof of Proposition 9.6

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Both formulas are present with the same constants and the same integrand; the only gap between the display and the Lean is what realizes T_0. 𝒫_new = ∫⟨g_r,new⟩_Y dR is `pressureMass` literally (torus average, then radial integral). g_r,new - ρ𝒫_new is `pressureSource` literally, with `rho` a normalized bump of unit radial mass supported in [a,b]. T_0 is realized as `RadialPullback.physicalCompact`, the compactly supported radial primitive in the pullback coordinate rather than a symbol named T_0; what I checked is the characterising identity `meanPressure_radial_residual`, which gives ∂_R(meanPressure f) - f = -ρ·pressureMass f - pressureAlias. That is the paper's T_0 property, with an extra `pressureAlias` term coming from the chart pullback that the display does not show. That `g_{r,new}` is the source of the *updated* state is supplied by `reconstructPressure`, which applies `meanPressure` to `u.gr c n` after the increment.
